Answer: B
Reason: Pulmonary aplasia is a congenital absence of lung tissue and its associated vasculature; the definitive radiographic sign distinguishing it from acquired causes of an opaque hemithorax (like total atelectasis) is the absence of the ipsilateral pulmonary artery. While mediastinal shift and compensatory hyperinflation occur in both aplasia and severe collapse, the missing vascular structure confirms the congenital agenesis/aplasia diagnosis.
